title: Deterministic invoice-line merging and consistent usage timestamp bucketing for billing exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customers intermittently report small invoice diffs and surprising line counts after exports to Stripe/NetSuite. Investigation shows two separate but interacting issues: (1) inconsistent bucketing of usage events (ingestion_time vs reported_usage_time, minute vs hour truncation, TZ handling) causes identical usage to be split across invoice lines, and (2) the invoice-line merge heuristic is non-deterministic under high-volume windows which leads to inconsistent dedup/merge decisions and rounding drift across retries. This ticket implements deterministic bucketing and a robust, idempotent merge strategy plus a backfill for affected invoices.
investigation:
- Data sampling across late-arrival windows (2025-01-15..2025-02-01) shows ~0.4% of usage events had usage_timestamp older than ingestion_timestamp by > 2 minutes; many came from mobile SDK with local clock skew.
- Export pipeline trimmed timestamps to hour boundaries in some batches and minute boundaries in others (legacy code paths).
- Merge logic relied on unordered set iteration when grouping by billing_key and unit_price; on replays this produced different merge groups.
- Round-trip local tests reproduce small rounding offsets on invoices when multiple merges occur and the order changes.
- No single incident spike; spread across many customers leading to many small diffs.
- Linked artifacts: billing-export debug logs, netstat of export worker runs, sample invoices attached in Confluence.
root_cause: A combination of inconsistent timestamp truncation rules between ingestion and export stages and a non-deterministic merge algorithm. Late-arriving events were occasionally bucketed into adjacent invoice line windows or left as orphan lines; the merge pass then produced non-repeatable merges depending on iteration order leading to rounding differences across export runs.
proposed_solution:
1) Standardize on UTC-aligned 60-second bucketing for usage events stored in the canonical usage table. All ingestion paths must write 'usage_bucket_utc' = floor(usage_timestamp to minute, UTC). Add an 'ingest_ts' column to preserve arrival order.
2) Change invoice-line merge to a deterministic algorithm: sort candidates by (billing_key, usage_bucket_utc, rate_id, quantity_desc, ingest_ts) before grouping; merge only adjacent sorted candidates that match merge predicates. Use integer cents arithmetic and explicit tie-breaking rules to avoid floating rounding differences.
3) Add feature flag 'deterministic_invoice_merge' to flip rollout.
4) Backfill job: generate reconciliation export for invoices in range 2025-01-01..2025-02-10 where exported_total != recomputed_total OR exported_line_count != recomputed_line_count; create controlled re-exports (idempotent) and raise customers with >$5 discrepancy.
5) Add schema migrations and tests to ensure bucketing is applied at ingestion and not re-truncated later.
rollout_plan:
- Week 1 (canary): Enable deterministic merge behind flag for 5% of exporters and run side-by-side comparison metric.
- Week 2 (expand): 25% traffic, monitor invoice deltas and export failure rates.
- Week 3: flip flag for all exports and run backfill job in low-traffic windows.
- Post-rollout: keep 'legacy_merge' code guarded and remove after 8 weeks if metrics stable.
Notes: Backfill will be rate-limited and run with idempotency keys to avoid double-charging. NetSuite/Stripe connectors will be called only for invoices that actually change.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for bucketing and deterministic sort/merge with randomized ordering invariants.
- Integration test: replay real usage slices including late-arrivers and clock-skewed events; assert export determinism over 5 replays.
- Staging dry-run: run new export job and compare CSVs vs current export; validate line_count, total_cents equality.
- Canary: send re-export for non-prod customers and surface UI diff in Console.
- Add golden tests that assert no float-based rounding in cents math.
- QA checklist to validate NetSuite mapping for merged lines and Stripe invoice line idempotency.
monitoring:
- New dashboard: 'Export Delta %' per account and per hour; alert if delta > 0.5% over 1h for >10 customers.
- Metric: 'export_line_count_change' (gauge) per invoice; alert on >2 changes post-export.
- Slowdown/lag monitors for backfill job.
- Logs: structured export diffs written to s3 path and referenced in incident tickets.
- Pager rule: only for production-wide regressions; individual customer diffs go to billing-review queue.
notes: We prioritized deterministic behavior over micro-optimizations that previously allowed faster merges; cost impact negligible compared to mis-invoicing risk.
Coordination with Payments team required before re-export to Stripe to ensure idempotency semantics.
Edge-case: leap-second handling — we will floor to minute epoch seconds (UTC) which is stable; added unit test for leap-second adjacent events.
